## Champion selection (D4 — measured, not defaulted)

- D4 default absent evidence: `logistic_regression`
- Measured champion (this project's own metric hierarchy, paired 5-fold CV): `random_forest`
- Paired t-test (n_folds=5): recall p=0.0086, F1 p=0.0166 — **low statistical power by construction** (only 4 degrees of freedom on a 5-fold paired test); treated as real, reproducible, directionally-consistent evidence for THIS dataset, not as license to over-claim certainty beyond it.

## Oracle external validation

| | Internal holdout | Oracle (external) |
|---|---|---|
| ROC-AUC | 0.794 | 0.463 |
| PR-AUC | 0.545 | 0.055 |
| Confusion matrix @ operating threshold (0.44) | — | TN 14497 / FP 0 / FN 923 / TP 0 |

Oracle ROC-AUC bootstrap 95% CI: [0.443, 0.481] (n_boot=1000) — statistically distinguishable from random — the CI does NOT contain 0.5, so this is measurably below chance, not merely indistinguishable from it.

**Statistical caveat (SH-05):** Oracle's 15,420 rows give this comparison high statistical power for what it measures — but PR-AUC's own baseline shifts with class prevalence (this project's internal fraud rate is 24.8%; Oracle's is far lower), so the internal-vs-Oracle PR-AUC gap above is not read the same way ROC-AUC's fixed 0.5 random baseline is — part of the gap reflects prevalence, not model degradation alone. The primary, prevalence-independent evidence for the generalization failure is the SHAP-weight constant-feature analysis in docs/REBUILD_NOTES.md (Oracle has no equivalent field for most of the model's top-weighted features), not the PR-AUC number alone.
